sections.heading: A vivid identity. A considered product.
sections.text: The owner-selected colorful mascot and RareIQ wordmark establish this identity. Expressive color creates recognition; precise typography, generous space and restrained applications establish its premium character.

sections.heading: The purpose of this book
sections.text: Use these standards across product, publishing and creator materials. The restored mascot and outlined wordmark are v2 production adaptations of the selected concept. Preserve the original reference as provenance. This book does not certify feature availability or release readiness.

title: Built around the creator
lead: RareIQ is the premium collectible/card recognition and intelligence product within Producer, Please.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Help creators bring collectible and card information into their production workflow. Feel capable, welcoming and attentive to the details of discovery and review.

sections.heading: Character
sections.text: Curious in discovery. Composed in operation. Expressive at the right moment. Premium quality comes from clarity, care and consistency.

sections.heading: Positioning
sections.text: Producer, Please is the parent live-production environment. RareIQ contributes its distinct collectible intelligence identity within that broader creator experience.

sections.heading: Signature
sections.text: Write RareIQ and RareIQ OCR exactly. Retain the comma in Producer, Please. Use Intelligence for creators as the tagline.

title: One identity, clear roles
lead: Producer, Please is the parent environment. RareIQ retains its own recognizable identity within it.

sections.heading: Producer, Please
sections.text: The parent live-production environment supports the overall creator workflow. This package supplies RareIQ identity assets; it introduces no parent logo.

sections.heading: RareIQ OCR
sections.text: RareIQ / RareIQ OCR is the premium collectible/card recognition and intelligence product. Use the same mascot and wordmark with OCR as a separate descriptor. Branding does not establish particular OCR capabilities or release readiness.

sections.heading: Card Studio
sections.text: Card Studio names a specialist workflow where present in the implementation. Preserve existing access and data; brand architecture alone does not change functionality.

sections.heading: Packaging
sections.text: Premium positioning does not establish prices, subscriptions, entitlements or launch commitments. Confirm availability before publishing claims.

title: The intelligence with a face
lead: Preserve the original mascot's silhouette, expression and distinctive color relationships.

sections.heading: Recognizable anatomy
sections.text: Preserve the rounded brain-like form, curved folds, cyan lower-left lobe, warm crown, two dark oval eyes with highlights, and three energy accents.

sections.heading: Expression
sections.text: Alert, curious and approachable. Suggest helpful intelligence while keeping the creator’s work central.

sections.heading: Master integrity
sections.text: Use the supplied restored master, a v2 production adaptation. The supplied flat and monochrome versions are authorized companion artwork. Preserve their defined forms; do not redraw, mirror, dress or change their expressions. Retain the original reference as provenance.

sections.heading: Presence
sections.text: Feature the mascot at introductions and welcoming moments. Let operational information lead during production.

title: A flexible logo family
lead: Choose the supplied composition that fits the available space.

sections.heading: Primary signature
sections.text: Use the mascot above the wordmark for hero applications. Add the tagline only where it remains comfortably readable.

sections.heading: Compact signature
sections.text: Use the horizontal composition in headers and shallow spaces. Omit the tagline when space is constrained.

sections.heading: Independent elements
sections.text: Use the mascot for icons and familiar navigation contexts. Use the wordmark alone where the context establishes RareIQ. The supplied Poppins-derived outlined wordmark is the v2 production adaptation; use its master instead of reconstructing it.

sections.heading: Descriptors
sections.text: Keep OCR and approved descriptors separate from the wordmark. Preserve supplied hierarchy and spacing; descriptors must not compete with RareIQ.

title: Give the mark room
lead: Size for recognition first. Remove supporting detail before reducing the mark further.

sections.heading: Clear space
sections.text: Define x as one-quarter of visible mascot height, excluding transparent padding. Keep x clear around the complete signature. For a standalone wordmark, use half the capital I height.

sections.heading: Digital starting limits
sections.text: Minimum widths: stacked 180 px; horizontal 160 px; OCR horizontal 320 px; tagline signature 320 px. Use the full mascot at 48 px or larger. Select dedicated favicon exports for smaller placements and inspect at actual size.

sections.heading: Physical reproduction
sections.text: Start at 30 mm width for a signature, or 55 mm with tagline. Increase for absorbent paper, embroidery or difficult processes. Approve suitability through a physical proof.

title: Control the surroundings
lead: A clean surrounding field lets the mascot's color carry the expression.

sections.heading: Dark and light
sections.text: Use the light wordmark on Deep Space and the dark wordmark on Paper. Preserve the supplied mascot colors and keep its outline clearly separated.

sections.heading: Photography
sections.text: Choose an uncluttered area or solid brand panel. Keep faces, meaningful artwork and essential production information clear.

sections.heading: Misuse
sections.text: Do not stretch, rotate, crop, recolor parts, change eyes, replace lettering, or add outlines, shadows or glow. Avoid busy or equally saturated surrounding fields.

sections.heading: One-color use
sections.text: Use the supplied monochrome companion for restricted reproduction. It is an authorized adaptation, distinct from the rendered master. Confirm readability with the intended process.

title: Color with intent
lead: Quiet foundations support a vivid spectrum of creator energy.

sections.heading: Foundations
sections.text: Deep Space #080F1A is the primary dark field. Paper #F7F8FC is the light foundation. Let neutral surfaces dominate.

sections.heading: Expression
sections.text: Purple #A855F7, Pink #FF4EDB, Orange #FF9F43, Cyan #00E5FF and Mint #7CFFCB are supporting accents. Preserve the mascot’s supplied shading.

sections.heading: Gradients
sections.text: Use cyan–purple–pink for selected cool accents and purple–pink–orange for warm expressions. Keep gradients away from long text, dense tools and critical status information. Never recolor the mascot with them.

sections.heading: Proportion
sections.text: Begin with a mostly neutral layout, choose one dominant accent and use the remaining spectrum sparingly.

title: Confident, readable type
lead: Poppins provides the supporting typographic voice; the supplied wordmark remains artwork.

sections.heading: Family and weights
sections.text: Use the supplied Poppins Regular 400, Medium 500, Semibold 600 and Bold 700. Avoid synthetic weights. Provide system sans-serif fallbacks during loading.

sections.heading: Reading rhythm
sections.text: Start body copy at 16 px with approximately 1.5 line height. Aim for 45–75 characters per line and a consistent heading hierarchy.

sections.heading: Tone
sections.text: Prefer sentence case. Reserve tracked capitals for short editorial labels. Keep paragraphs left aligned and compact controls readable.

sections.heading: Practical use
sections.text: Keep ordinary text live where practical. Retain the supplied font license and confirm embedding permissions. Use the supplied outlined logo master; do not rebuild it with typed lettering.

title: Clarity is a brand behavior
lead: Expressive accents must coexist with understandable, usable production controls.

sections.heading: Text and contrast
sections.text: Test actual foreground/background pairs, including gradients and interaction states. No accent is automatically suitable for every text size or surface.

sections.heading: Meaning
sections.text: Assign functional success, warning, error and information roles. Pair color with labels or icons. Brand color alone must never imply verified readiness.

sections.heading: Interaction
sections.text: Preserve keyboard focus, semantic labels, adequate targets and useful disabled-state explanations. Keep important text outside image-only artwork and provide meaningful alternative text.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.text: Review dark/light themes at 1080p, 4K and narrow desktop widths. Check zoom, long labels and reduced motion before claiming accessibility conformance.

title: Speak with calm confidence
lead: Make the next useful action clear, and describe the evidence honestly.

sections.heading: Voice
sections.text: Use plain language, concrete verbs and short sentences. Be welcoming in introductions and precise in operations. Avoid effortless or flawless outcome promises.

sections.heading: Brand examples
sections.text: Intelligence for creators. Collectible intelligence within Producer, Please. Make room for your next discovery. These express positioning, not feature guarantees.

sections.heading: Operational examples
sections.text: Reading text… Check the extracted text before using it. Text recognition is unavailable. Use each message only when it describes the implemented state.

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text: Distinguish planned, experimental, locally tested and platform-verified capabilities. Avoid universal compatibility, guaranteed recognition or native broadcasting claims without evidence.

title: Space creates distinction
lead: Build a clear sequence: one message, one visual focus, one next action.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.text: Use a consistent grid, generous margins and an 8 px spacing rhythm. Establish reading order; group related content through alignment and proximity.

sections.heading: Surfaces
sections.text: Keep interface surfaces quiet. Use restrained depth and borders to clarify structure. Reserve large color fields for brand-led moments.

sections.heading: Imagery
sections.text: Show real creator contexts and truthful product captures. Preserve complete subjects and useful detail. Let abstract color support the message without obscuring the product.

sections.heading: Format
sections.text: Compose landscape and portrait separately. Preserve faces, logos and critical text. Label conceptual interfaces and illustrative applications when they could be mistaken for shipped functionality.

title: Motion with a purpose
lead: Movement should explain change and preserve the operator's attention.

sections.heading: Brand motion
sections.text: Prefer a short fade or small positional entrance of the complete signature. Preserve anatomy. Avoid distortion, flashing, indefinite bouncing and decoration during critical tasks.

sections.heading: Reduced motion
sections.text: Honor reduced-motion settings. Provide static equivalents and keep progress understandable without movement.

sections.heading: OCR state language
sections.text: Where implemented, distinguish ready, reading, review, confirmed, unavailable and failed. Detected text or confidence estimates do not establish verified identity or transactions.

sections.heading: Honest feedback
sections.text: Show measured progress only when supported; otherwise use a labeled working state. Preserve recovery actions. Avoid celebrating accuracy before review. These are design standards, not claims of implemented OCR states.

title: Recognizable wherever it appears
lead: Adapt the same identity to the context and the viewer's distance.

sections.heading: App and avatar
sections.text: Center the mascot on a clean field. Keep its face and accents within safe areas. Inspect square, rounded and circular crops at final size.

sections.heading: Social and presentation
sections.text: Pair one concise message with the signature. Reserve space for platform controls and framing. Preserve the brand hierarchy.

sections.heading: Documents
sections.text: Use a distinctive cover, quiet interior typography and consistent page furniture. Avoid repeating a large mascot on every page.

sections.heading: Streaming
sections.text: Compose landscape and portrait slates with clear safe zones. Keep permanent marks modest. Sample overlays do not demonstrate encoder integration, audio playback or destination receipt.

title: A careful handoff
lead: Choose the right file for the medium and preserve the provenance of the master.

sections.heading: Digital files
sections.text: Use PNG for rendered mascot artwork and SVG for genuine vector components. A bitmap embedded in SVG remains raster. Label that distinction in the inventory.

sections.heading: Resolution
sections.text: Choose sufficient native pixels for final placement. Upscaling does not restore detail. Inspect edges and eyes at actual output size.

sections.heading: Print
sections.text: Hex colors specify RGB. Saturated accents may shift in printing. Agree on the printer’s output profile and substrate, then approve a physical proof. Do not claim universal CMYK or spot-color matches.

sections.heading: Package
sections.text: Deliver book, sources, assets, tokens, font/license notes and inventory. Identify masters, provenance, production limitations and illustrative applications.

title: Keep the identity coherent
lead: Version the system, preserve its masters and keep every public claim tied to evidence.

sections.heading: Ownership
sections.text: The owner selected the colorful mascot direction. This v2 system defines its production adaptations and companion artwork. Signal Cut remains historical.

sections.heading: Asset control
sections.text: Select files through the inventory. Separate masters from exports and document material changes. New variants require a deliberate design decision; users should not reconstruct supplied masters.

sections.heading: Product rollout
sections.text: Package delivery differs from application integration. Update shared tokens, logos, manifests and identity checks together. Verify the running interface across supported themes and viewports.

sections.heading: Release discipline
sections.text: Record created, checked and untested layers. Preserve permissions and provenance. Public publishing, deployment and paid activity require separate authorization.
